questions.text: Let [latex]\Sigma[/latex] be a finite non-empty alphabet and let [latex]2^{\Sigma^{*}}[/latex] be the power set of [latex]\Sigma^{*}[/latex] . Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] can be listed in order of length (then dictionary order), so it is countably infinite.

[latex]2^{\Sigma^*}[/latex] is the power set of a countably infinite set, which is uncountable (Cantor's theorem).

Answer: [latex]2^{\Sigma^*}[/latex] is uncountable and [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] is countable

questions.text: One of the purposes of using intermediate code in compilers is to
questions.solution:
Intermediate code is machine independent. The same optimizer (and front end) can be reused with different back ends for different machines.

Answer: increase the chances of reusing the machine-independent code optimizer in other compilers

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
1) Static allocation of all data areas by a compiler makes it impossible to implement recursion.
2) Automatic garbage collection is essential to implement recursion.
3) Dynamic allocation of activation records is essential to implement recursion.
4) Both heap and stack are essential to implement recursion.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 1: With static allocation each function has one fixed data area, so recursive calls overwrite it [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- 2: Garbage collection is not needed for recursion [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False.
- 3: Each call needs its own activation record created at run time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- 4: A stack alone is enough; a heap is not needed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False.

Answer: 1 and 3 only

questions.text: In the context of modular software design, which one of the following combinations is desirable?
questions.solution:
Good modules do one job well (high cohesion) and depend little on other modules (low coupling).

Answer: High cohesion and low coupling

questions.text:
A system uses 3 page frames for storing process pages in main memory. It uses the Least Recently Used (LRU) page replacement policy. Assume that all the page frames are initially empty. What is the total number of page faults that will occur while processing the page reference string given below?
4, 7, 6, 1, 7, 6, 1, 2, 7, 2
questions.solution:
LRU with 3 frames:

- 4, 7, 6: faults (3)
- 1: fault, evict 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {7, 6, 1} (4)
- 7, 6, 1: hits
- 2: fault, evict LRU 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {6, 1, 2} (5)
- 7: fault, evict 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {1, 2, 7} (6)
- 2: hit

Answer: 6
